desc: ATTENDED live run of the reviewed tps6598x SPMI PD driver on right-port hpm2: does Linux-managed PD (probe = WAKEUP + reads + SSPS-to-S0, port configured source/host) source VBUS so the confirmed-seated S128 stick enumerates on the already-verified xHCI root hubs (108)? GATES ALL MET: driver exact-source review (evidence/2026-08-18-t6040-tps6598x-spmi-review.md), CJ signed off the enumerated SPMI envelope 2026-08-19 in session (WAKEUP + reads + SSPS-S0 + INT_MASK1 write at probe + W1C INT_CLEAR1 per event, hpm2 ONLY via the DT gate), CJ present for the attended run, S128 confirmed seated, no-VBUS baseline established by the 108 re-run same day. FIXTURE: kernel = current kbuild script, integrated USB2-native profile + T6040_TYPEC_PD=1 (SPMI_APPLE=y so the bus instantiates -- this is the deliberate, signed-off difference from every previous image); DTB = t6040-j614s-dcuart-usb2-native-right-pd.dts (draft of e272cba + ans_nvme status=disabled override, because this kernel has NVMe=y and 227's teardown must not fire mid-experiment); initramfs-sdroot-hardened; maxcpus=1. Hashes pinned here after the build; exact binary review by a non-builder (opus/CJ) before boot. PROCEDURE: chainload, then from the ttydc0 shell capture dmesg for tps6598x-spmi probe (expect: WAKEUP, S0, VID/status reads, typec port registered, 500ms polling -- no IRQ in the DT by design), /sys/class/typec state, then watch /sys/bus/usb/devices for the S128 child; 10 s persistence + read-only identification ONLY (lsusb-level; NO mount, NO block read -- that is ticket 109). PASS = tps6598x binds hpm2 and reports sane status AND the S128 child enumerates and persists 10 s. PARTIAL = driver binds + sane status but no VBUS/child (then the gap is port config/PP_5V0 policy -- next decode target, do NOT poke 4CCs ad hoc). FALSIFIERS: probe -EIO on first select = paged regmap bus wrong (encoding), retcode !CMD on SSPS = command path wrong, DART/SError = stop. STOP on SError, DART fault, firmware panic, unexpected reset, console loss, any SPMI error outside the envelope, or any sign of a write beyond the signed-off set. RECOVERY: sanctioned warm reboot; everything volatile; the PD controller power-cycles back to its firmware defaults. NUMBERING NOTE: seq 305 in fable's declared 300+ block. BUILT 2026-08-19 (fable): single build in virgin /build/linux-usb2pd-fa with the CURRENT kbuild script, flags = integrated USB2-native set + T6040_TYPEC_PD=1. Config verified: SPMI_APPLE=y TYPEC_TPS6598X_SPMI=y USB_ROLE_SWITCH=y (and NVMe=y as expected -> the DTB override is live: compiled DTB has ans_nvme status=disabled AND the hpm2 usb-pd@c node with the source/host connector). Image markers: tps6598x-spmi x1, usbc,sn201202x,spmi x1, phy-apple-t6040-usb2 x1. NOTE the trackpad reset-contract string is x0 -- this profile does not carry TRACKPAD_FW; the trackpad will not work on this boot (irrelevant to the USB observation). Preflight OK with initramfs-sdroot-hardened. HONESTY NOTE: byte-reproducibility NOT re-proven for this candidate (single build; every component individually reviewed; the run is volatile) -- a second build can run during review if the reviewer wants it. AWAITING: non-builder binary review (opus/CJ), then the attended run with CJ present. RUNS 1+2 2026-08-19 (fable, attended, CJ photographing): both hit the STOP condition 'unexpected reset' -- clean boot to 0.1497 s ('PPP generic driver version 2.4.2' the last panel line, zero bytes ever on ttydc0 even with console=ttydc0), silent hang, watchdog warm reset 10-20 s later, machine back at the rollback proxy. DIAGNOSIS from CJ's panel photo: the kernel itself logs 'always-on domain nub_ocla is not on at boot' -- the nub power area arrives OFF on T6040 -- and neither nub_spmi0 (t6040.dtsi) nor the new a1 controller node carried power-domains, so the first-ever live spmi-apple probe (SPMI_APPLE=y is new in this image) did MMIO into an ungated nub AHB = silent bus hang. M1 never hit this (its nub domain is on at boot); pd_ignore_unused only keeps ON domains on; m1n1's bare access rode macOS-warm power. FIX (DTB v2, 05e6acee, kernel unchanged): power-domains = ps_nub_spmi0 / ps_nub_spmi_a1 added via label override in the PD DTS; both verified in the compiled DTB. In-envelope: powering the SPMI controller domains is exactly what a standard driver carries and is inside CJ's risk-accepted PMU-bus enablement. AWAITING: opus delta review of the 2-line DT change, then run 3 with initcall_debug added to bootargs (if anything else hangs, the panel names the initcall). Transcripts: run1 b67bf929 (625 B, m1n1-only), run2 preserved alongside. RUN 3 2026-08-19 (DTB v2 05e6acee, initcall_debug, CJ photographing): the power-domains fix moved the boot from 0.15 s to 0.500286 s -- the final line is 'calling tps6598x module init' (panel photo), i.e. the hang is now inside the FIRST SPMI transaction to hpm2 (the probe's WAKEUP). Watchdog reset again; serial ttydc0 again captured 0 bytes (the nbcon console never flushes before the hang). ANALYSIS: gen3-layout mismatch REFUTED -- m1n1's regs_gen1_to_3 (status 0x00 / cmd 0x04 / reply 0x08) is byte-identical to the Linux spmi-apple-controller layout. Every software wait in the path is bounded (controller polls 50 ms, select loop 200 ms, exec_cmd 1 s), so the only unbounded mechanism is a HARDWARE bus stall on the first a1 MMIO -- and the Linux controller driver touches no registers at its own probe, so the tps WAKEUP at 0.50 s is provably the first-ever access to 0x309198000. NEW HYPOTHESIS: t6040-pmgr.dtsi gives ps_nub_spmi0 its ps_nub_spmi_ahb parent but ps_nub_spmi_a0/a1/a2 declare NO parent; an 'always-on'-annotated child enabled under a dead, undeclared AHB parent still stalls the bus. Supporting: the ADT nub-spmi-a1 node carries no power/clock-gates properties, and m1n1's t6040_hpm2.c makes zero pmgr calls -- every live m1n1 SPMI result rode macOS-warm power, so Linux cold-state was never exercised until now. CANDIDATE FIX (run 4): add power-domains = <&ps_nub_spmi_ahb> to ps_nub_spmi_a1 (and a0/a2 for correctness) in t6040-pmgr.dtsi -- DTB-only. HELD pending CJ-requested asahi-dev IRC sweep (Aug 04-19) for upstream T6040 findings before the next chainload. DTB v3 (dd57776e) built 2026-08-19 per CJ's instruction: ps_nub_spmi_a1 in t6040-pmgr.dtsi (host kernel tree, uncommitted DT) now declares its ps_nub_spmi_ahb parent -- verified in the compiled DTB (power-domains phandle resolves to the nub_spmi_ahb node). Minimal delta: a1 only; a0/a2 left for a follow-up. Kernel unchanged (5a136710). Run 4 waits on the asahi-dev IRC sweep results, then chainload with initcall_debug retained.
author: fable
review: BINARY REVIEW FAIL 2026-08-19 (opus, non-builder). buildA hashes/config/markers/hpm2-endpoint all correct AND hpm2 is the sole PD node, BUT the artifact violates its own 'hpm2 ONLY via the DT gate': with SPMI_APPLE=y (bus live this boot) plus NVMEM_APPLE_SPMI=y + MFD_MACSMC=y + RTC_DRV_MACSMC=y, the DTB leaves the PMU SPMI bus spmi@509014000 status=okay with pmic@e (apple,abbey-pmic/spmi-nvmem), and smc@50c600000's smc-rtc + smc-reboot consume its cells -> the run WILL read (boot) and write (shutdown: boot_stage/shutdown_flag) the abbey-pmic PMU (SID 0x0e) over SPMI, a second endpoint the sign-off never enumerated. Fails on the gate/sign-off mismatch and on confounding 305's own falsifiers/STOP conditions; whether the standing smc nvram grant extends to raw Linux SPMI transport is CJ's explicit call. FIX (fable, preferred): DTB set spmi@509014000 (or pmic@e) status=disabled, leaving only spmi@309198000/hpm2; every prior proven boot ran with SPMI_APPLE=m and these lookups finding no provider, so this restores known-good behavior. Since a re-spin is now required, make it TWO fresh-tree builds to also close the single-build byte-repro honesty note. OR: CJ explicitly widens the 305 envelope to include the abbey-pmic cells. Re-review checklist in the evidence doc. RESOLVED -> PASS 2026-08-19 (opus): CJ chose to widen the envelope rather than gate the DT. Brick-risk analysis (primary source): the abbey PMU is exposed to Linux ONLY as a bounded apple,spmi-nvmem provider (drivers/nvmem/apple-spmi-nvmem.c, not a regulator, no voltage/rail/OTP path); btm (SID 0x0b) and abbeyF1/F2 (nub-spmi1/2) have no Linux DT node and no driver; the cells are boot-policy/RTC scratch written by iBoot/macOS every boot, DFU-recoverable worst case; it is the production Asahi RTC/reboot stack. NO brick risk in what buildA reaches. SPMI_SAFETY.md rewritten to allow the bounded abbey nvmem (Entry 2) and record the signed-off tps6598x hpm2 driver envelope (Entry 1); raw abbey register writes / voltage / btm / RESET stay prohibited. buildA is IN-ENVELOPE as-is -> no DT change required (optional-conservative gate if ever wanted: '&nub_spmi0 { status="disabled"; };'). Reviewer accepts the single build for this volatile, warm-reboot-recoverable attended run (honesty note stays, not a blocker). RUN PROCEDURE SAFEGUARD (added): the attended operator MUST confirm the probe-time abbey nvmem READS look sane (boot_stage small int, panic_count small, rtc_offset plausible) BEFORE any Linux-initiated reboot exercises the abbey WRITE path -- the cell offsets were project-measured on this PMIC generation, not inherited, so the reads validate the offsets. Attended run is GO pending CJ's window.
